headline: Oxa already knows curation is the bottleneck (they blogged about multimodal search); the open gap is turning found scenarios into synced 3D plus 2D labels fast enough to keep pace with new port, airport and Dubai deployments.
what_they_build: Oxa sells a "universal AI driver" for industrial vehicles: self-driving software, modular up-fit hardware and fleet management for terminal tractors, tugs and yard vehicles in ports, airports and factories. Buyers are logistics and infrastructure operators such as DHL (Heathrow), bp and Port of Tyne, plus the new Dubai Future Foundation joint venture. Revenue is per-site deployment and per-fleet software, so each new site is a new data domain.
inferred_pipeline: Multi-camera plus LIDAR (and likely radar, GNSS, CAN) recorded from safety-driver and autonomous runs on repetitive site routes; logged to object storage, probably AWS or Azure (guess).

Ingest and triage inside Oxa Foundry: disengagement and trigger-based clip extraction, plus the multimodal search capability described in their October 2025 blog (confirmed they have some form of search, scope unknown).
Clip selection for labelling, probably a mix of engineer intuition and rule-based triggers; sent to an outsourced labelling vendor or in-house team (guess).
Annotation of 3D cuboids on point clouds and 2D boxes/masks on synced camera frames, with calibration-driven projection between them (guess on how sync is enforced).
Perception model training and evaluation, likely on NVIDIA stack given the September 2025 NVIDIA expansion; validation against safety cases for each site.
Shadow-mode or on-vehicle replay, failures fed back as new triggers; loop closure time unknown.

hypotheses.pain: Each new site (Heathrow, Port of Tyne, Dubai) is a fresh domain with different vehicles, markings and weather, forcing a new labelling push instead of reusing an existing corpus.
hypotheses.evidence: Site-specific wins listed on their news page: DHL Heathrow, Port of Tyne, Dubai JV; messaging is "any industrial vehicle" across ports, airports and yards.
hypotheses.encord_answer: Index registers the new site's data in Oxa's own bucket, embeds it, and similarity search against existing clips shows what is genuinely novel versus already covered. Collections feed straight into Annotate workflows, so only the new slice gets labelled.

hypotheses.pain: Synced 3D point cloud plus multi-camera labelling is slow and expensive, and inconsistency between the cuboid and the 2D box shows up as perception errors late.
hypotheses.evidence: Our read of their sensor stack; no public detail. Their own framing of "safe, explainable" autonomy implies heavy validation evidence per object class.
hypotheses.encord_answer: Annotate handles 3D point cloud / LIDAR and native video in one ontology, with object tracking and interpolation across frames and sampled review routing. Agents can run Oxa's own detector as a pre-labelling stage so annotators correct rather than draw.

hypotheses.pain: Hard to prove which data to label next: disengagements and triggers find obvious failures but not the quiet long tail (low sun, fog, hi-vis staff at range) that drives safety case gaps.
hypotheses.evidence: Blog "Accelerating self-driving software development with multimodal search" shows they are investing here; SWIR / adverse-conditions research interest in the signal list.
hypotheses.encord_answer: Active imports Oxa's predictions and correlates data metrics with model failures, so you can slice mAP by class, IoU threshold, brightness or site and get a ranked list of what to label next. It also surfaces label errors before they reach training.

ontology.name: Terminal tractor / reach stacker / forklift
ontology.why: Primary dynamic obstacles in yards and ports; need range and heading for planning.

ontology.name: ISO container / trailer / dolly
ontology.why: Static-but-movable structures that define drivable corridors and docking manoeuvres.

ontology.name: Ground crew in hi-vis
ontology.why: Vulnerable road user class; the safety case depends on long-range detection.

ontology.name: Aircraft and ground support equipment
ontology.why: Irregular silhouettes at airside; boxes over-cover and waste free space.

ontology.name: Drivable surface and apron markings
ontology.why: Free-space segmentation for confined yard routes with painted lanes.

ontology.name: Lane, stop line and quay edge
ontology.why: Thin linear geometry; polylines keep labels cheap and precise.

ontology.name: Dock door / charging bay keypoints
ontology.why: Precise docking and alignment targets for final-metre manoeuvres.

ontology.name: Scene conditions (fog, low sun, night, rain, site)
ontology.why: Lets Active slice model performance by condition and site for the safety case.

case_study.name: Automotus
case_study.why_it_matches: Fixed-infrastructure cameras watching repetitive vehicle movement in a constrained zone, same shape of problem as a port yard or airside apron: lots of near-duplicate frames, a thin long tail that actually matters, and cost per labelled frame under pressure.
case_study.numbers: +20% mAP, 35% smaller training dataset, 33% lower labelling cost after curating with Encord. Encord also claims 60-80% labelling cost reduction on high-complexity use cases with automation plus active learning.

proof_of_value: Week 1, day 1-2: register one site's logs (say Port of Tyne or a Heathrow airside route) from Oxa's own S3 or Azure bucket into Index. Data never moves. Success: embeddings and quality metrics on 100% of frames within 48 hours.

Week 1, day 3-5: build the ontology above with Oxa's perception lead and run de-duplication plus diversity sampling across three repeat passes of the same route. Success metric: frames to label cut by 50% or more while keeping 95% of distinct scenes, benchmarked against Oxa's own selection for the same batch.

Week 2, day 1-3: label the curated slice in Annotate with synced LIDAR cuboids and camera boxes/masks, using interpolation and tracking, plus an Agents stage running Oxa's existing detector for pre-labels. Success: measured minutes per clip versus their current baseline, and review pass rate.

Week 2, day 3-4: import Oxa's current model predictions into Active on a held-out set. Success: a ranked metric-to-failure report naming the three conditions or classes driving most error (expect low sun, hi-vis pedestrians at range, occluded containers).

Week 2, day 5: train or fine-tune on curated versus random-equal-size picks and compare. Success: curated beats random on mAP50 at equal label spend, mirroring our own 0.48 vs 0.43 warehouse-robot result, plus a signed-off view on whether Encord complements or duplicates Oxa Foundry.
discovery_questions: Your October 2025 post on multimodal search: what did you build in Foundry, and where does it stop - is it search and triage only, or does it reach into labelling and model evaluation?
When you stand up a new site like the Dubai JV or Port of Tyne, how much of the labelled corpus from Heathrow actually transfers, and how do you decide what to re-label?
How are 3D cuboids on the point cloud and the 2D camera labels kept consistent today, and who catches it when they disagree?
What is the current path from a disengagement or shadow-mode failure to a labelled training example, and how many days does that round trip take?
Is labelling done in-house, by a vendor, or both, and what is the current cost and throughput per hour of sensor data?
risks: Oxa Foundry is their own toolchain and they have publicly written about multimodal search, so Index may be seen as duplicating something they already built and are proud of. Position around Annotate and Active first.
No ML or CV job ads found and no named contact, so we have no direct evidence of a tooling gap or an active buying trigger. Pain is inferred from their deployments, not stated.
Fresh $103m Series D first close means budget exists but also means they may prefer to hire and build rather than buy.
Safety-case and customer data agreements (DHL, bp, airport airside) could make even bucket-registered third-party access slow; expect security review despite SOC2 Type II and GDPR.
NVIDIA partnership expansion may pull them toward NVIDIA's own data tooling for the AV stack.
